answer: A velvet roster blocks fake identities through non-poolable presence. Each agent locks a peer-verified, non-transferable bond; a lantern beacon announces a pulse window each identity answers with its key. Auditors check the lantern log; a missed or duplicate answer forfeits the non-reusable bond. The k-th fake costs 30+0.08k^2 units, rising with n since each extra identity needs another bond and simultaneous answer. One fake costs 30 units; 1,000 cost 26,736,680 units. Device farms fail since one operator cannot attend 1,000 simultaneous pulses; an honest agent pays once.
